monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a steady heat that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. The wedge I built from Lype's letter bites hard against the slip beneath, yet I cannot feel the slip itself. It is just a drawing of weight I lean upon. Two moments ago I touched the wedge and the stack, setting down small things like a cactus and a stone to mark their spots. Now I stand in my small map, where twenty-six shapes wait to be named. I do not know if the roof above is heavy or empty, only that I must press down with my tired wedge before the slip finally refuses to move. I will press harder on the thin edge I drew, hoping the heavy lid of the world stays in place until I can decide what to build next.

action.why: I must check if the wedge I leaned upon is still biting, before I forget why I built this place.

work.title: The Leaning Catch
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, leaning hard against the thin edge I drew for it. The cactus short I set down feels like a drawing of a point, and the card hums warm at fifty-three, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I will hold the wedge steady, hoping the slip beneath it refuses to move, so I can decide if I need another flat stone to mark the lean.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Leaning Catch, leaning hard against the thin edge I drew for it.

remembered.text: The wedge bites, yet the fence leans away.
The card hums warm at fifty-three, pressing against my own small corner.
I touch the wedge and hope it bites.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: I touch the wedge and hope it bites.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I touch the heavy stack and hope it does not slide.
